_note: Seed of the project bases (phase 13.1, D303 to D307). Principle names follow TOGAF 10's example principles plus security ones; all wording is EA Explorer's own.

principles.name: Primacy of Principles
principles.statement: These principles apply to every organisation in the enterprise and to every architecture decision.
principles.rationale: Consistent decisions across the enterprise need one set of rules that everyone follows.
principles.implications: Exceptions go through the governance log as dispensations; projects state how they follow each principle.

principles.name: Maximise Benefit to the Enterprise
principles.statement: Decisions about information and technology aim at the greatest benefit to the enterprise as a whole.
principles.rationale: Local optimisation often costs the enterprise more than it saves one area.
principles.implications: Some areas give up preferences for the common good; priorities are set at enterprise level.

principles.name: Information Management is Everybody's Business
principles.statement: Everyone in the enterprise takes part in decisions about information management.
principles.rationale: Information serves the business, so the business must own what it needs from it.
principles.implications: Business people join architecture work and make time for it.

principles.name: Business Continuity
principles.statement: Business operations carry on despite failures of systems or services.
principles.rationale: Interruptions cost money, trust and regulatory standing.
principles.implications: Critical services have tested recovery; resilience is designed in, not added later.

principles.name: Common Use Applications
principles.statement: Applications used across the enterprise are preferred over ones built for a single area.
principles.rationale: Duplicate solutions cost more and give conflicting data.
principles.implications: Areas adopt shared applications unless a dispensation is granted.

principles.name: Service Orientation
principles.statement: The architecture is built from services that model real business activities.
principles.rationale: Services can be combined, reused and changed with less effort.
principles.implications: Business and application capabilities are exposed as services with clear contracts.

principles.name: Compliance with Law
principles.statement: Information management and its processes comply with all relevant laws, regulations and policies.
principles.rationale: Non-compliance brings penalties, harm and loss of trust.
principles.implications: Regulatory obligations are traced to requirements; changes in law are watched for.

principles.name: IT Responsibility
principles.statement: The IT organisation is responsible for owning and implementing IT processes and infrastructure that meet agreed needs.
principles.rationale: Clear ownership keeps cost, quality and timing under control.
principles.implications: IT delivers to agreed service levels; requests go through one intake and prioritisation.

principles.name: Protection of Intellectual Property
principles.statement: The enterprise's intellectual property is protected in the architecture, its solutions and its processes.
principles.rationale: Intellectual property is a source of advantage and value.
principles.implications: Policies and controls guard designs, data and code; third parties sign protective terms.

principles.name: Data is an Asset
principles.statement: Data is an asset that has value to the enterprise and is managed as such.
principles.rationale: Accurate, timely data underpins decisions; poor data costs money.
principles.implications: Data has owners, quality measures and investment like other assets.

principles.name: Data is Shared
principles.statement: Users can reach the data they need to do their work; data is shared across functions.
principles.rationale: One shared source is cheaper and more consistent than many copies.
principles.implications: Shared data stores and interfaces replace private copies; sharing rules are agreed.

principles.name: Data is Accessible
principles.statement: Data is accessible for users to perform their functions.
principles.rationale: Wide access makes the enterprise more efficient and responsive.
principles.implications: Data is easy to find and use, through tools and interfaces people understand.

principles.name: Data Trustee
principles.statement: Each data element has a trustee accountable for its quality.
principles.rationale: Someone must answer for whether data can be relied on.
principles.implications: Trustees are named; quality issues are routed to them and fixed at source.

principles.name: Common Vocabulary and Data Definitions
principles.statement: Data is defined consistently across the enterprise, in terms everyone understands.
principles.rationale: Shared definitions make data exchange and reporting reliable.
principles.implications: A business glossary and data dictionary are kept and used in every design.

principles.name: Data Security
principles.statement: Data is protected from unauthorised use and disclosure, by classification.
principles.rationale: Breaches harm people, the enterprise and its standing.
principles.implications: Data is classified; access, encryption and monitoring follow the classification.

principles.name: Technology Independence
principles.statement: Applications are independent of specific technology choices and so can run on several platforms.
principles.rationale: Independence keeps options open and lowers the cost of change.
principles.implications: Applications use standard interfaces and avoid proprietary lock-in where practical.

principles.name: Ease-of-Use
principles.statement: Applications are easy to use; the technology is transparent to the user.
principles.rationale: Usable systems need less training and fewer workarounds.
principles.implications: Common look and behaviour; usability is tested with real users.

principles.name: Requirements-Based Change
principles.statement: Changes to applications and technology are made only in response to business needs.
principles.rationale: Change driven by need keeps cost and risk down.
principles.implications: Every change traces to a requirement; technology refresh is justified by business value or risk.

principles.name: Responsive Change Management
principles.statement: Changes to the enterprise environment are made in a timely way.
principles.rationale: People need change fast enough to stay effective.
principles.implications: Change processes are quick and predictable; small changes go through a lighter path.

principles.name: Control Technical Diversity
principles.statement: Technical diversity is controlled to reduce the cost of maintaining many platforms.
principles.rationale: Each extra platform adds skills, support and integration cost.
principles.implications: A list of approved technologies is kept; new ones need a dispensation and a retirement plan.

principles.name: Interoperability
principles.statement: Software and hardware follow established standards that promote interoperability.
principles.rationale: Standards make components fit together and reduce integration effort.
principles.implications: Interfaces follow the standards information base; exceptions are logged.

principles.name: Cloud First
principles.statement: New platforms use cloud services unless there is a reason not to.
principles.rationale: Cloud services scale with demand and shorten delivery.
principles.implications: Each solution records its hosting choice and the reason for any on-premises exception.

principles.name: Secure by Design
principles.statement: Security is designed into solutions from the start, not added at the end.
principles.rationale: Fixing security late costs far more and leaves gaps.
principles.implications: Threat modelling and security requirements are part of every design; security reviews gate releases.

principles.name: Least Privilege
principles.statement: People and systems get only the access they need, for only as long as they need it.
principles.rationale: Limited access limits the damage of mistakes and attacks.
principles.implications: Role-based access, regular access reviews, and time-bound elevated rights.

principles.name: Defence in Depth
principles.statement: Several independent layers of control protect each important asset.
principles.rationale: One failed control should not expose the asset.
principles.implications: Network, identity, application and data controls all apply; no single control is relied on.

principles.name: Zero Trust
principles.statement: No user, device or network is trusted by default; every access is verified.
principles.rationale: Attackers inside the perimeter are a real and common risk.
principles.implications: Strong authentication everywhere, segmented networks, continuous checks on access.

principles.name: Privacy by Design
principles.statement: Personal information is protected by default across its life.
principles.rationale: Privacy laws and customers' trust require it.
principles.implications: Collect only what is needed, keep it only as long as needed, and record the lawful basis.

principles.name: Security Monitoring
principles.statement: Security events are logged, monitored and acted on.
principles.rationale: Attacks that are not seen cannot be stopped.
principles.implications: Central logging, alerting and an incident response that is practised.

standards.name: ArchiMate 4 for architecture models
standards.description: Architecture models use ArchiMate notation and concepts.

standards.name: BPMN 2.0 for process models
standards.description: Business processes are modelled in BPMN 2.0.

standards.name: Business capability modelling convention
standards.description: Capabilities are named as nouns, levelled to three levels and owned by a business area.

standards.name: Value stream mapping convention
standards.description: Value streams are described as stages from a stakeholder's trigger to the value delivered.

standards.name: Decision records
standards.description: Architecture decisions are recorded in the governance log with context, options and consequences.

standards.name: Business glossary and data dictionary
standards.description: Every shared data entity has an agreed definition, owner and trustee.

standards.name: Data classification scheme
standards.description: Data is classified as Public, Internal, Confidential or Restricted; handling follows the class.

standards.name: ISO 8000 data quality
standards.description: Data quality is defined and measured along ISO 8000 lines (accuracy, completeness, timeliness).

standards.name: ISO/IEC 11179 metadata registries
standards.description: Data elements are described with consistent metadata.

standards.name: ISO 8601 dates and times
standards.description: Dates and times are exchanged in ISO 8601 format, with time zones.

standards.name: UTF-8 character encoding
standards.description: Text is stored and exchanged as UTF-8.

standards.name: OpenAPI 3 for REST interfaces
standards.description: Synchronous interfaces are REST over HTTPS, described in OpenAPI 3.

standards.name: JSON for data exchange
standards.description: Interfaces exchange JSON unless a domain standard says otherwise.

standards.name: OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect
standards.description: Applications authenticate users and services with OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0.

standards.name: Event-driven integration with a message broker
standards.description: Asynchronous integration uses events on the enterprise broker, with schemas registered.

standards.name: Semantic versioning of interfaces
standards.description: Interfaces and packages carry semantic versions; breaking changes raise the major version.

standards.name: Containers to the OCI standard
standards.description: Applications are packaged as OCI containers and run on the approved orchestration platform.

standards.name: Infrastructure as code
standards.description: Environments are defined as code, reviewed and versioned.

standards.name: Supported operating systems: long-term support releases only
standards.description: Servers run long-term support releases still in vendor support.

standards.name: TLS 1.2 or later
standards.description: All network traffic is encrypted with TLS 1.2 or later.

standards.name: Approved cloud services catalogue
standards.description: Cloud services are chosen from the approved catalogue; others need a dispensation.

standards.name: ISO/IEC 27001 information security management
standards.description: The information security management system follows ISO/IEC 27001.

standards.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
standards.description: Security capabilities are organised by the CSF functions: govern, identify, protect, detect, respond, recover.

standards.name: OWASP ASVS for application security
standards.description: Applications are verified against the OWASP Application Security Verification Standard.

standards.name: CIS Benchmarks for hardening
standards.description: Platforms are hardened to the CIS Benchmarks.

standards.name: Encryption at rest: AES-256
standards.description: Confidential and restricted data is encrypted at rest with AES-256 and managed keys.

standards.name: Multi-factor authentication
standards.description: Access to systems holding confidential data needs multi-factor authentication.
